gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the omitted covolume factor in counting integer points of D0 and affine lattice sets. ISSUE-003 concerns an invalid modular-inverse construction in a subsignal lemma; it neither identifies the lattice-density normalization nor repairs the volume-to-lattice-point estimate.

The gold issue is the exclusion of required boundary coefficient vectors from D_gamma because of a strict norm inequality, including the gamma=±1 vectors. ISSUE-003 addresses invertibility of k/d1 modulo the wrong modulus and does not recognize the boundary-domain omission or its deterministic contribution to rho.

The gold issue is the false global perturbation bound for the truncated lattice vector and the need to use a projected top-block estimate. ISSUE-004 concerns a prime-factor case split in dynamic-programming iteration ordering, with no diagnosis of coordinatewise truncation error or rounding control.

The gold issue is an algorithmic candidate-recognition test that compares a truncated coordinate with the exact value ±beta0 instead of ±floor(beta3 beta0)/beta3. ISSUE-001 is a Fourier nonzero-frequency gcd criterion and scaling error, so it does not diagnose the incompatible SVP coordinate test.

The gold issue is the unjustified substitution of an expected value of K for a deterministic worst-case runtime bound. ISSUE-004 concerns whether a corrected subproblem appears in an earlier dynamic-programming iteration and does not identify the probabilistic-versus-worst-case runtime inference.

Both identify the same numerical-reporting defect: the successful 11×13 experiment used 16 of 143 coefficients, about 11.2%, not 8 of 143, about 5.6%, so the comparison with 350/3600 about 9.7% is reversed. The prediction also gives the corresponding repair to reconcile the prose with the table and remove or reverse the claimed advantage.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The reported 11×13 coefficient count and resulting percentage comparison are inconsistent with the table; correcting the count changes the comparison from an asserted advantage to 11.2% versus 9.7%.

component_coverage.gold_component: The 11×13 successful inversion used 16/143≈11.2%, not 8/143≈5.6%, and therefore does not use a smaller fraction than the 60×60 case at 350/3600≈9.7%.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly computes the table-supported count as 16, derives 16/143≈11.2%, observes that this exceeds 9.7%, and specifies correcting or withdrawing the claimed percentage advantage.
